findings.finding: The UTF-8-validity heuristic is not bug-for-bug. Go's trim loop (charset.go:81-90) scans back at most 3 bytes and cuts at the FIRST RuneStart byte (utf8.go:457: `b&0xC0 != 0x80`) WITHOUT checking whether the rune is complete — so a complete trailing 2- or 3-byte rune is trimmed, which can drop hasHighBit to false and route the WHOLE page to windows-1252 (charset.go:91-103). The port's `_trim_partial_trailing_rune` (:246-263) instead compares `len(data) - i < expected` and keeps complete runes. Probed against a faithful re-implementation of charset.go:52-104: ASCII + trailing 'é' -> Go windows-1252 vs Python utf-8 (same for a trailing 3-byte rune; 4-byte, partial-rune, and invalid cases agree). Observable whenever the trailing rune is the only high-byte content in the 1024-byte preview: Go emits mojibake for the entire document, the port emits clean UTF-8. Not on the FIX-FORWARD list, so §0 requires bug-for-bug.
findings.citation: x/net@v0.58.0 charset.go:80-90 (trim at first RuneStart, no completeness check) + :91-103; /opt/homebrew/Cellar/go/1.27.1/libexec/src/unicode/utf8/utf8.go:457 (RuneStart); inventory.tsv row 49 item (4) ("trim partial trailing rune" — under-specified wording the implementation followed; rulebook preamble: "The old code is the spec"); RULEBOOK §0 ("Everything NOT on this list ports bug-for-bug")

findings.finding: Unknown/unsupported charset labels in a meta tag abort the whole extraction where Go falls through. `_prescan_meta_charset` (:284-286) returns any non-empty charset label verbatim; probed: `<meta charset="made-up-charset-xyz">` returns the label, `_decode` then raises LookupError, wrapped as ValueError('charset detection: ...') and swallowed by handle() into '' — i.e. webfetch succeeds with empty text. Go's prescan (charset.go:194-197) sets needPragma but leaves e nil on Lookup failure and only returns `if e != nil` (:209), so the scan CONTINUES and the page decodes via the utf-8 heuristic / windows-1252 default, producing text. Related and unaddressed: there is no WHATWG(htmlindex)-vs-Python-codec label equivalence layer, so label-set mismatches have the same abort behavior. This also falsifies the code's own comment (:86-88) that charset decode failures are "near-unreachable in the port" — this path makes them reachable while Go's charset.NewReader only errors on reader failure (charset.go:108-119), which cannot happen for bytes.
findings.citation: x/net@v0.58.0 charset.go:194-197 + :200-211 (failed Lookup does not return; prescan continues) and charset.go:108-119 (NewReader error is reader-only); inventory.tsv row 49 item (3) + its TODO scope ("attribute quoting edge cases, tentative-UTF-16 NUL sniff" — unknown labels and label mapping are neither named nor decided anywhere) ; RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule + §5 (undecided site: flag it, TODO(port), most-conservative translation)

findings.finding: The meta prescan is a regex over latin-1 text, not the tokenizer prescan the row cites, and diverges on input classes the row never decided. Probed: (a) a commented-out `<!-- <meta charset="utf-16"> -->` returns utf-16 — Go's prescan sees only StartTagToken/SelfClosingTagToken (charset.go:142-146) and CommentToken falls through the switch, so the meta is invisible; (b) `<meta charset="utf-16">` inside `<title>` returns utf-16 — x/net's tokenizer treats title/textarea/script/style/noscript/iframe/noembed/noframes/xmp as RCDATA (token.go:849 `case 't': raw = z.startTagIn("textarea", "title")`, :1042-1055), so no StartTagToken is emitted; (c) `content="text/html; charset =windows-1251"` returns None — Go's fromMetaElement trims " \t\n\f\r" before the '=' (charset.go:219-228) and yields windows-1251; (d) '>' inside a quoted attribute truncates the regex match and the charset is lost. The TODO(port) at :277 covers only "attribute quoting edge cases" and "tentative-UTF-16 NUL sniff", which does not reach comments, RCDATA, or whitespace-before-'='. The code comment's claim of "tokenizer document order" (:276-277) is inaccurate — no tokenizer is used.
findings.citation: x/net@v0.58.0 charset.go:139-146 (prescan switch handles only start/self-closing tags) + charset.go:216-247 (fromMetaElement whitespace rules); x/net@v0.58.0 html/token.go:849 and :1042-1055 (RCDATA raw-text tags incl. title); inventory.tsv row 49 item (3) + TODO scope; RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule (unlisted construct -> flag for the §2 table)

adherence: Did the implementer follow the rulebook? Mostly yes on the mechanical/structure dimension, with two process violations and two parity divergences the inventory under-decided. VERIFIED COMPLIANT (source-read, probes where executable): (1) §5/rows 47-56 — every looked-up site matches its inventory row: three raise sites byte-shaped per row 47 with raise-then-swallow kept honest (raise at :162, swallow at :70-71, `except Exception` not BaseException); cleanDocument two passes with the 31-entry and 3-entry selector lists proven identical to Go after whitespace normalization (row 48); findMainContent 6-entry priority verbatim, first-match, best-div strictly-greater byte length first-max-wins, body-None fallback with a TODO(port) (row 51); title = concat of ALL <title> matches, meta description first-match-only with exists/empty semantics (row 55); Each loop: name -> get_text(separator=\"\") -> html.unescape -> strip -> BYTE length (unescape BEFORE trim per rows 50/53, postprocessor.go:68); pre/code >=10 gate before dedup, inline `>=5 and code` with no trailing separator (the s07-pinned nested-code quirk), h* `if raw` + level map with Go zero-value `.get`, default branch minTextLen 20 + 'Read more' prefix; dedup as a shared set[str] of raw text (row 52); (2) BYTES-CHARSET row 49 + conflict C-1: the §1 charset row is overridden by the row per conflicts.md (\"implementers follow the row, not §1\", amendment A-1 queued) — BOM table exactly 3 entries in x/net order (charset.go:250-257), 1024-byte window, pragma-form http-equiv requirement correct (probed: X-UA-Compatible rejected, attr-order-agnostic, cp1251 fixture resolves windows-1251), windows-1252 default; (3) §6 trailer accurate: 2 TODO(port) markers = todos=2, no undercount; §3 marker format correct, no unmarked type:ignore/cast; §4 import style (absolute, qualified) correct; §1 sync service layer, bs4+html.parser choice, `str` internally/`bytes` at the boundary — all per §1. ROW-SANCTIONED DEFERRALS (not findings): utf-16-from-meta remap absent (probed) but inside row 49's TODO scope; strip() vs TrimSpace U+001C-001F divergence acknowledged in rows 50/53. DEVIATIONS: the two rule-violations above (missing postprocessor.py import target — §4/manifest/§0; bs4 never declared/installed — §1 deps/§0 referee), plus the three divergences where the implementation went past or short of Go on inputs the rows left undecided or under-worded (trailing-rune trim; unknown-label abort; regex-vs-tokenizer prescan gaps). The practical effect of the process violations: I could not execute any bs4-dependent path (cleanDocument/findMainContent/Each loop end-to-end); the attempted end-to-end diff of rich.html against the pinned s07 capture (639-byte text) failed at import, so those subsystems are verified by source diff against goquery semantics and the row-cited probes only, not by execution. Per standing bans I ran no builds and no tests; all probes were python3 -c with stdlib stubs, plus file reads.
